title: Wire a recoverable measurement chain
intro: Build a telemetry chain whose recorded output can be inverted back to the original angle. Two wirings are forbidden — and they are the two ways invertibility dies.
briefing: A control surface angle θ is read by a periodic resolver, digitised, and logged; a solver must later reconstruct θ from the log. The inspector rejects any chain where the resolver reaches the digitiser without passing through a domain restriction (a periodic reading is many-to-one — the angle is unrecoverable), and rejects any chain containing a saturating amplifier at all (past its stop, every larger input maps to one output, and nothing downstream can undo that).

rules.label: The angle is read by the resolver
A periodic reading is invertible only on one restricted branch
The branch-restricted signal is what gets digitised
The solver works from the telemetry log
No unrestricted periodic reading: many-to-one, so θ is unrecoverable
No saturating stage anywhere: saturation destroys injectivity for good

debrief:
The winning chain is θ → resolver → restriction → digitiser → solver, and both forbidden wirings are the same theorem wearing different clothes: **a composite is invertible only if every stage stays injective**.

Wiring the resolver straight to the digitiser is the periodicity failure from Chapter 2. A resolver reading 30° cannot be distinguished from 390° or 750°, so the log contains a value with infinitely many preimages. The domain restriction is not a filter or a clean-up step — it is what *creates* the bijection, exactly as restricting sine to [-π/2, π/2] is what makes sin⁻¹ exist at all.

Placing the saturating amplifier anywhere is the failure from Chapter 1's hydraulic ram. Past its stop, every larger input produces the same output; the preimage stops being a value and becomes a set. Note that the rule bans it from the board entirely rather than just from the solver's wire — because saturation upstream is equally fatal, and 'it isn't directly connected to the solver' is precisely the reasoning that puts unrecoverable data in a flight recorder.

The general move: before building a chain you intend to invert, name every stage that could go many-to-one — saturation, quantisation, modular wraparound, ratios that discard signs — and either keep it out of the recorded path or restrict its domain until it is one-to-one.
